A.explanation: Path A curves to the left in the plane of the paper, in the same direction as the electric field in diagram 1. An electron has negative charge so the force $F = qE$ is opposite to the field.

B.explanation: In diagram 1 the field acts to the left in the plane of the paper, so the force on the negative electrons acts to the right, producing the in-plane deflection to the right shown by B.

C.explanation: Path C is an in-plane deflection, but in diagram 2 the field is into the paper so the force $F = -eE$ is out of the paper and cannot produce curvature confined to the plane of the paper.

D.explanation: Path D is an in-plane deflection, but in diagram 2 the electric force is perpendicular to the plane of the paper, so the beam would be deflected out of the plane, not along D.

hints: Notice the field direction in diagram 1 is to the left in the plane of the paper while the electrons enter moving upwards.
Recall the electric force is $F = qE$, and for an electron $q = -e$, so the force direction is opposite to the electric field direction.
Compare diagram 2, where the field is into the paper, and ask whether a force into or out of the paper can cause the in-plane curves C and D.
walkthrough: Identify the two cases: diagram 1 has $E$ to the left in the plane of the paper, diagram 2 has $E$ into the paper perpendicular to the plane. Electrons enter both fields moving upwards.
State the rule for the force: $F = qE$, where the electron charge is negative. The force on the electron is therefore in the opposite direction to $E$.
Apply to diagram 1: $E$ left means $F$ right. A rightward force acting at right angles to the initial upward velocity gives projectile-like curvature to the right in the plane of the paper.

Apply to diagram 2: $E$ into the paper means $F = -eE$ out of the paper. This force is perpendicular to the plane of the paper, so it would deflect the beam out of the plane, not along an in-plane curve such as C or D.
Therefore only diagram 1 can give one of the drawn in-plane paths, and the rightward deflection is the curve labelled B. This is option B.
